clue.text: Number of goods transported out of France

indicators.note: taking something out of a thing leaves the rest behind, so letters are removed

parts.note: goods carried by lorry, ship or train
FR is the standard abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: A customs officer counts how many consignments of goods left France.
explanation.walkthrough: FREIGHT loses its FR to leave EIGHT; 'Number' looks like a count of shipments but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a cardinal numeral, one of the counting words.

clue.text: Energy company records temperature to inspire one environmentalist

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside another

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
standard abbreviation for company
a log is a written record
T is the symbol for temperature
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An energy firm keeps temperature records hoping to win over a green campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: E and CO come first, then LOGS plus T, i.e. LOGST, breathes in I to make LOGIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecologist studies how living things relate to surroundings, and the word is commonly used for a green campaigner.

clue.text: Doctor going on vacation early billed UK resident

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
a vacated house is emptied, so the word loses everything between its ends

parts.note: the word with its insides emptied out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A GP who slipped off on holiday early has billed a British patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a GP and 'billed' like invoicing, but the doctor shuffles letters and 'billed' means having a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a wild goose that breeds in Britain, and as a bird it has a bill, so it is a billed resident.

clue.text: Trifle cheers date

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks
D is the abbreviation for date; that the clue word itself ends in these letters reversed is a coincidence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' looks like the British pudding, but here it means a small amount; 'cheers' is thanks, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle and a tad both denote a very small quantity, as in 'a trifle cold'.

clue.text: Promotes unique en suite stores

indicators.note: a thing that stores something keeps it inside, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A shop chain pushes its distinctive bathroom fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an advert, with 'Promotes' as marketing; really it is chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a pawn reaching the last rank is promoted, usually to a queen, so to queen a pawn is to promote it.

clue.text: File one used to break out of trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so whatever comes out of it is spoken

parts.note: a snooker player uses a cue to break, the opening shot

explanation.surface: A prisoner hides a file to break out of a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' looks like a tool for a jailbreak and 'break out' like an escape; break is the opening shot in snooker, and trap means mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a line of people one behind another, the same as a line waiting their turn.

clue.text: Dress up bride more fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants the bride decked out even more elaborately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a comparative for the bride's dress, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a story is to embellish it with invented detail, which is figuratively dressing it up.

clue.text: American candy requires core to be made right

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, and making it into something else replaces that letter

parts.note: to require is to need
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sweet from the US has to have its centre made properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of NEEDS is its middle letter, the second E; it becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerds are small, crunchy, tangy sweets made in the United States and sold in boxes.

clue.text: Cry of son the same after dropping ecstasy

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: ecstasy is E in drug slang, and in a down entry dropping a letter moves it lower, changing the order

parts.note: equal means identical in value

explanation.surface: A parent's cry about a son who is unchanged after giving up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping ecstasy' looks like quitting the drug, but in this down entry the E slides lower in its word rather than vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeal is a high-pitched shriek, a kind of cry.

clue.text: Lacking any guts, endeavour to bung me in lake

indicators.note: to bung is to chuck or toss carelessly, so the letters land in a jumble
with all its insides gone only the two ends of the word survive

parts.note: the first and last letters only
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spineless effort to throw someone into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bung me in' reads as throwing a person into water; bung here mixes up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is an old and poetic English word for a lake or pond, found in place names such as Windermere.

clue.text: Release version of song for two barely behind schedule

indicators.note: bare means stripped, so the outer coverings of the words come off

parts.note: a cover is a new release of an existing song by another artist
a duet is a piece for two performers

explanation.surface: A cover of a duet comes out just a little late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to modify 'behind schedule' but it strips COVER DUET of its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue describes something that has not arrived or happened by its expected time, i.e. late.

clue.text: Short noble in Lyon that is flamboyant

indicators.note: a short version is cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman
que is French for 'that', Lyon being a French city

explanation.surface: A diminutive aristocrat in Lyon cuts a showy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' seems to describe a small noble but trims BARON; 'in Lyon' tells you to translate into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque is the highly ornate seventeenth-century style, and by extension means extravagant and showy.

clue.text: Order soldiers away from alcohol inside? That's not right

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: something sent away from a thing is no longer in it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: liquor is strong drink
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Commanding troops to stay off the drink inside — someone objects that this is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not right' sounds like a protest at the order, but it is geometry. OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblique line or angle is slanting, neither perpendicular nor a right angle, so it is not right in the geometric sense.

clue.text: Vibrate small particle without resistance back in institute

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so a letter goes

parts.note: a quark is a subatomic particle
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter only

explanation.surface: A physics lab test shakes a tiny particle with no resistance at the back of an institute.
explanation.walkthrough: QUARK drops R to make QUAK, then the end of 'institute' supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: To quake is to shake or tremble, as the ground does in an earthquake.

clue.text: Out of bounds area not suitable for children

parts.note: OB is the golfing abbreviation for out of bounds
a scene is a field or sphere of activity, as in the music scene

explanation.surface: A sign marks a forbidden zone that is unsafe for kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one restricted place; it splits after 'bounds' and again after 'area'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is offensively indecent, the kind of content kept away from young people.

clue.text: Stuck fast at home reading novel

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in the house, absorbed in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being read, but it signals the rearrangement of 'reading'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrained habits or dirt are fixed firmly and deeply, so hard to remove.

clue.text: Drinkers here prepared big lunch, scoffing tons

indicators.note: to scoff food is to gobble it down, so one piece is swallowed by another
prepared food has been worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Pub regulars here laid on a huge lunch and ate masses of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinkers here' is a cryptic pointer to a place where people drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a late-night venue for dancing where patrons buy alcohol, so drinking happens there.

clue.text: Divorce leads to tummy aches, leaving aunt queasy

indicators.note: the leading letters are the ones at the front of each word

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A messy split gives a stomach ache to an aunt who is left feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a family drama; only the word starts matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Talaq is the Islamic form of divorce in which a husband repudiates his wife, so it names a divorce.

clue.text: Arctic forest thawing every so often north of America

indicators.note: something happening every so often occurs at intervals, so letters are taken at regular gaps

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Northern woodland is gradually thawing above America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'north of' means placed above, i.e. before.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast belt of coniferous woodland bordering the tundra in subarctic regions.

clue.text: Search about to stop is creating problems

parts.note: a quest is a search

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so one piece fills the middle of another

parts.note: taken as written
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A search that is about to be halted is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to stop' reads as imminent halting, but 'about' supplies letters and 'to stop' plugs them into 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Questions in the sense of issues or matters needing solving are problems, as in 'the Irish question'.

clue.text: Hat and necklace jeweller ultimately junked

indicators.note: something junked is thrown out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a torque, or torc, is a metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter counts

parts.note: the last letter only

explanation.surface: A jeweller's hat and necklace were eventually thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat and necklace' reads as a pair of items, but 'and' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, and also the tall white hat chefs wear.

clue.text: Quality Assurance Agency checking books, students at the front go far using them?

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: QAA is the UK body that monitors university standards
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter only

explanation.surface: University inspectors audit the books while students up front head off somewhere distant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a cryptic definition: an airline is what you use to travel far, especially to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Qantas is Australia's national airline, famed for very long-haul flights, so passengers use it to travel great distances.

clue.text: Begin to grow first sign of grey fur around bare pate

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter only

indicators.note: a piece placed around another encloses it

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

indicators.note: stripped bare, a word loses its outer letters

parts.note: the inner letters only

explanation.surface: A balding man starts growing grey fuzz around his bald crown.
explanation.walkthrough: A pate is the top of the head, and 'bare' strips its outside rather than describing baldness.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed germinates when it sprouts, i.e. starts developing into a plant.

clue.text: Vibrant iguana sheltering somewhere in the Caribbean

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A brightly coloured lizard takes cover on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The iguana tempts you to shuffle its letters, but the answer runs on from the end of 'Vibrant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is an island in the eastern Caribbean, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Sweet affectionate soldier

parts.note: fond means loving
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so soldier often means ANT

explanation.surface: A kind, loving soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the soldier, but it is the noun meaning a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugar paste used for icing and in confectionery, and a fondant is a sugary sweet.

clue.text: After reflection, headquarters provided understanding religious law

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is flipped, so the order runs backwards

parts.note: standard abbreviation for headquarters
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Having thought it over, the head office agreed on the meaning of the religious rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflection' looks like 'on consideration' but means written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiqh is Islamic jurisprudence, and the Arabic word literally means deep understanding.

clue.text: Concur with adult longing to be rid of daughter

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: getting rid of something means removing it

parts.note: greed is a strong desire
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Siding with a grown-up who wants the daughter out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concur with' reads together, but 'with' only links definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share an opinion, the same as to agree.

clue.text: Players square off with sides before international game, wanting third place

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter in position three goes

parts.note: the inner letters only

explanation.walkthrough: 'Players square off' looks like a confrontation, but players is the definition and SQUARE loses its sides; TEST drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is a group of four musicians, and musicians who perform are players.

clue.text: Intelligence turned up note claiming bishop's praying this way

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held inside

B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Spies dig up a memo stating that the bishop prays in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: QI and LA together hold B; the 's stands for 'is' and links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face for prayer.

clue.text: Scrap bolt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fight or row
second meaning: a short heavy arrow fired from a crossbow

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs (throw away, run off), but each is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heated argument and the square-headed missile shot from a crossbow.

clue.text: New boy garb?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A Babygro is a stretchy all-in-one sleepsuit for infants, so clothing for a newborn child.

clue.text: Grill toppings for beef burgers quickly

indicators.note: the topping of each word is what sits at its head, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Grill some toppings for beef burgers in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toppings' looks like burger garnishes, but it means the tops of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: BBQ is the usual abbreviation for barbecue, an outdoor grill.

clue.text: Rodent's sudden movement when dodging king snake

indicators.note: to dodge something is to avoid it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a jerk is a quick sharp movement

a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa is a desert-dwelling rodent of Africa and Asia with long hind legs for jumping.

clue.text: Muscles shown by cycling team

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so a letter moves from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a squad is a team
